chadi-init.description: Initialize or refresh the current repo with agent-chadi workflow files.
chadi-init.template: Use agent-chadi. Initialize this project if missing: detect the stack, package manager, test/lint/build commands and key directories, then record them in the project's rules file (AGENTS.md or the harness equivalent) and create the workflow state directory (.opencode/chadi). If already initialized, refresh only what is missing. Do not create files for other harnesses.

chadi-fast.description: DEFAULT mode. Main-agent-first workflow. Standard work auto-proceeds; Heavy work waits for approval unless pre-approved.
chadi-fast.template: Use agent-chadi. chadi-fast mode (Workflow v2): classify the lane first. 3 or fewer known files: edit inline, one targeted verify, no dispatch. 4+ files: write the context pack (ctx-<slug>.md) and the frozen contract (contract-<slug>.md), then dispatch all independent lanes as parallel calls in ONE block, each brief ending with the turn-economy footer. Never poll long-running work. Audit only for sensitive or unreadable diffs. Report Changed / Files / Verified / Skills / Blocked with real command output. Heavy work waits for approval unless user already pre-approved.

chadi-review.description: Run final testing, security review, and code review.
chadi-review.template: Use agent-chadi. Run testing review, security review, and final code review of the current changes. Report findings with evidence and update the .opencode/chadi logs when they exist.

chadi-plan.description: Create an industry-style plan with risk classification and parallel execution plan.
chadi-plan.template: Use agent-chadi. Do intake, acceptance criteria, discovery, architecture map, risk classification, and PARALLEL_PLAN.md (lanes, disjoint file ownership, contract and context-pack steps). Use matching skills and available LSP/ast-grep/context7 tools when relevant. Do not implement yet unless the user already asked to proceed.

chadi-waves.description: Plan a multi-layer feature as parallel waves (contract -> builders -> integration -> verify -> deploy) and dispatch wave 0.
chadi-waves.template: Use agent-chadi. Call plan_feature with the user's request as the goal (tool names are bare; OpenCode prefixes graphyloop_, Claude Code mcp__graphyloop__). Report the wave table (which lanes run in parallel, what each owns, what gates the deploy). Wave 0 writes the context pack (ctx-<slug>.md) and the frozen contract (contract-<slug>.md) alone. Then pass plan.tasks to task_distribute and dispatch ONLY the tasks it returns in dispatchNow. After each result, task_record it and dispatch whatever that unblocked, all tasks of a wave in ONE parallel call. Every lane brief ends with the turn-economy footer. Do not let a builder start before the contract and ctx files exist. Never poll.

chadi-db.description: Set up or migrate the database (Supabase-first): check credentials, plan migrations, dry-run before apply.
chadi-db.template: Use agent-chadi. Database setup lane (tool names are bare; OpenCode prefixes graphyloop_, Claude Code mcp__graphyloop__). 1) secrets_status to see which Supabase keys exist — never ask the user to paste a key into the chat; if one is missing, tell them the exact key name and where to get it, then store it with secrets_set. 2) env_sync so the app reads real credentials from its own env file. 3) preflight target=db and clear every blocker. 4) Write schema changes as migration files (never dashboard-only edits), with RLS policies and indexes. 5) Run the dry-run step and show its SQL BEFORE any apply; the apply step needs explicit user approval and a rollback note. Never print a credential value.

chadi-deploy.description: Ship to Vercel safely: preflight, mirror env keys, preview deploy, then gated production.
chadi-deploy.template: Use agent-chadi. Deploy lane (tool names are bare; OpenCode prefixes graphyloop_, Claude Code mcp__graphyloop__). 1) preflight target=deploy — every blocker must be cleared first (missing VERCEL_TOKEN, no build script, env file not git-ignored). 2) Mirror every runtime env key in the Vercel project; a local .env.local is not deployed. 3) Apply pending database migrations before the app deploy, dry-run first, with a rollback note. 4) Run the local build, then a PREVIEW deployment and verify the real URL, waiting with the tool's blocking command (never a sleep loop). 5) Production deploy only after explicit user approval, and record the rollback command in the report. Never print a credential value.

chadi-audit.description: Run testing, security, performance, and final code review without broad implementation.
chadi-audit.template: Use agent-chadi. Audit the project or current changes. Run testing review, security review, performance/reliability review when relevant, and final code review. Report findings with evidence and update the .opencode/chadi logs when they exist.

chadi-release.description: Prepare release notes, rollback plan, and final verification summary.
chadi-release.template: Use agent-chadi. Prepare release notes, rollback plan, risk register update, verification summary, and final checks for the current work.

chadi-skills.description: Check which bundled and referenced skills are installed for this harness.
chadi-skills.template: Use agent-chadi. Run skills_status and inspect the skill directories this harness reads (project-local skills, the user-level skills directory, and any harness-specific location). Report which bundled and referenced skills are installed and which are missing. Do not fake missing skills.

chadi-research.description: Use last30days for fresh public internet/community research before answering.
chadi-research.template: Use agent-chadi. Use the installed last30days skill as source-of-truth for fresh public internet research. Research the user's topic from the last 30 days, then answer with a grounded summary and cite/summarize the evidence. If last30days is missing or fails, report that and use the closest available fallback (official docs, web fetch).

chadi-confusing.description: For confusing/current questions, research first using last30days, then answer.
chadi-confusing.template: Use agent-chadi. The user is asking something confusing or likely recent. Before answering, check whether last30days is installed. If available, use it to research current public context. If not available, say what fallback you used. Then answer clearly.

chadi-discuss.description: Discuss-first mode: parallel discovery then present plan, wait for approval before implementing.
chadi-discuss.template: Use agent-chadi in DISCUSS-FIRST mode. Inspect only needed files with batched tools. Present a concise plan: lane chosen, what I'll do, files touched, approach, risks, optional parallel work if warranted, and verification plan. WAIT for user approval before implementing. Do NOT implement until the user says go/proceed/approved.

chadi-go.description: Skip discuss gate, straight to main-agent implementation.
chadi-go.template: Use agent-chadi. User pre-approved — skip the discuss gate. Classify the lane: 3 or fewer known files go inline; 4+ files get a context pack and frozen contract, then ONE parallel wave of disjoint lanes (each brief ends with the turn-economy footer). Run tests and a diff review once after the lanes land, audit only if the change is sensitive, and report Changed / Files / Verified / Skills / Blocked with real output.

chadi-recall.description: Memory recall — search graphyloop memory for facts, lessons, decisions and past activity.
chadi-recall.template: Use agent-chadi. Call memory_search with 2-4 keywords from the user's topic (tool names are bare; OpenCode prefixes graphyloop_, Claude Code mcp__graphyloop__), optionally filtered by type (decision, lesson, pattern, event). Synthesize the results and say which entries informed the answer. If nothing is found, say so; never fabricate a memory.
